before.title: Rectangular PEC guide and cavity geometry, the zero-normal-B reflection class, and axis-relative TE/TM/TEM
before.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its frame basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, its SI units and its fields $E,B$ be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]] and [[def-em-fields]]. Fix $a,b>0$, write $x_t=(x_1,x_2)$, $e_z:=e_3$, and define $\nabla_t f=(\partial_1f,\partial_2f,0)$, $\Delta_t f=\partial_1^2f+\partial_2^2f$ and $\operatorname{div}_tu_t=\partial_1u_1+\partial_2u_2$ for the stated regularity, using [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].
(a) [Straight guide] A straight guide region is $\Omega_A:=A\times\mathbb R$ where $A$ is either a bounded connected $C^1$ plane domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) or the explicit rectangular cross-section; the rectangle has corners and is treated by its open faces, not asserted to be a $C^1$ boundary domain, with longitudinal axis $e_z$; for a rectangular cross-section $A=R_{ab}:=(0,a)\times(0,b)$ the region is called the rectangular guide and its walls are the four open faces $\{x_1=0\},\{x_1=a\},\{x_2=0\},\{x_2=b\}$. A rectangular cavity region is $\Omega_c:=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times(0,d)$ for fixed $d>0$, with the six open faces as its walls. The separate smooth-cavity spectral branch uses an explicitly declared bounded $C^\infty$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ with its smooth PEC boundary; it is not the rectangular reflection class. Spatial derivatives are taken at fixed $t$; the fields are defined on $\Omega\times I$ with the regularity declared by each theorem.
(b) [PEC boundary model] On every open wall (a wall minus its edges) the ideal perfectly conducting boundary model declares the two conditions $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$, where $n$ is the outward unit normal of that wall ($-e_1,+e_1,-e_2,+e_2$ on the four rectangular walls, and $\pm e_j$ on the six cavity walls). Its physical reading is the ideal-conductor limit of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]: with $E=B=0$ inside the ideal conductor the tangential electric field and the normal magnetic field vanish, while the surface-charge and surface-current readings $n\cdot D=\sigma_f$ and $n\times H=K_f$ are determined by the traces and are not prescribed here. The supplier's hypotheses (a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with one-sided $C^1$ fields) cover a smooth stationary interface, not the $\sigma\to\infty$ idealization nor the box edges; the guide/cavity conditions on the open walls are therefore declared as an idealization of this definition, and no pointwise statement on the edges is made.
(c) [Zero-normal-B reflection class] For the rectangular box $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L=(a,b,d)$, the reflection class is the class of locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $Q$ whose extensions to the rectangular torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$, defined by extending $E_1$ evenly across the $x_1$-walls and oddly across the $x_2$-, $x_3$-walls and cyclically for $E_2,E_3$, and extending $B_1$ oddly across $x_1$ and evenly across $x_2,x_3$ and cyclically for $B_2,B_3$, are $L^2$ fields, together with the distributional constraints that $\operatorname{div}E$ and $\operatorname{div}B$ vanish on the torus for the extensions. This is the declared weak PEC model used for the cavity initial-value problem; for smooth fields the parities give $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$ on $\partial Q$. Initial data not in this class (for example data with trapped normal $B$) are excluded, as are the general $H(\operatorname{curl})$ boundary classes, which are defined by the mathematical suppliers and are not identified here with the classical conditions.
(d) [TE, TM, TEM] For a guide or cavity field $(E,B)$, the longitudinal components are $E_z:=E\cdot e_z$ and $B_z:=B\cdot e_z$; the field is called TE (transverse electric) if $E_z\equiv0$, TM (transverse magnetic) if $B_z\equiv0$, and TEM if both vanish, always relative to the named axis $e_z$.
(e) [Separated phasor convention] For $\omega>0$ and $\beta\in\mathbb C$, a $\beta$-$\omega$ separated phasor field on the guide is a real field of the form $F(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\tilde F(x_1,x_2)e^{i(\beta x_3-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with a complex amplitude $\tilde F$, componentwise; $\omega/(2\pi)$ is the frequency and $\beta$ the longitudinal propagation constant; when $\beta$ is real, $\beta>0$ describes propagation in the $+e_z$ direction under this phase convention, while a complex $\beta$ gives the spatial factor $e^{-\operatorname{Im}\beta x_3}$ and may grow in the opposite direction; each consuming branch states its selection.
(f) [Scope] The definition fixes the geometry, the PEC boundary model, the weak reflection class and the mode terminology; it asserts no field equation, no constitutive law and no existence or completeness of modes, Rectangular TE/TM candidates and the rectangular reflection class, declared smooth bounded PEC cavity spectral classes, and smooth straight-guide TEM potential branches (including the coaxial annulus) are within this geometry. No general non-rectangular TE/TM guide theory, circular-guide spectral classification, open-end or junction scattering, or lossy model is supplied.
before.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: geometry and transversality are fixed by coordinates and normals; the PEC model is declared with its interface reading and its excluded idealization/edges; the reflection class is defined by the reflection rules and distributional divergence constraints; the phasor convention is stated as an encoding of real fields. No differential equation is introduced.
before.physical_scope: The ideal PEC boundary model of the straight rectangular guide and cavity (and of straight guides with a bounded connected C1 cross-section) in the lossless laboratory chart, together with the zero-normal-B reflection class and the TE/TM/TEM classification. The boundary model is an idealization of an interface with a perfectly conducting medium on the open walls; the definition asserts no field equations, constitutive laws or mode completeness.

after.title: Constant-Ohmic PEC modal decay and exact energy-class completeness
after.statement:
Assume the constant isotropic inertial-rest material branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $\sigma\ge0$, $D=\varepsilon E$, $H=B/\mu$, $J_{\rm ext}=0$. The exact broadband physical reading additionally requires $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$ as in that closure; otherwise the positive coefficients define its finite-band effective phase model without a universal front-speed claim. Put $v^2=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}$ and $\gamma=\sigma/\varepsilon$. The smooth equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] with initially zero volume charge give $E_t=v^2\operatorname{curl}B-\gamma E$, $B_t=-\operatorname{curl}E$ and zero divergences; in the finite-energy classes below these first-order equations with the declared PEC weak/variational boundary realization are adopted explicitly, rather than deduced from a smooth-only postulate. The quadratic stored energy is $\mathcal U(t)=\tfrac12(\varepsilon\|E(t)\|_2^2+\mu^{-1}\|B(t)\|_2^2)$, consistent with [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]].
(a) [Rectangular cavity] In the exact zero-normal-$B$ reflection-parity and divergence class of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] and [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]](c), every initial pair has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ distributional solution of this damped system in the same class. Finite Fourier mode sums converge in energy norm uniformly on compact time intervals and are dense at every time. The Fourier coefficient equations at $k_j=\pi n_j/L_j$ are $\widehat E_t=iv^2 k\times\widehat B-\gamma\widehat E$, $\widehat B_t=-ik\times\widehat E$, with both transverse constraints and the original parities retained.
(b) [Smooth closed PEC cavity] Assume the full Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the smooth spectral and elliptic suppliers. On a bounded smooth cavity $\Omega$, let $X,V,H$ and its smooth orthonormal eigenfields $u_j$, $\lambda_j\ge0$, be exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] and [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]. Define the full weak normal-zero divergence-free magnetic space $$M:=\{B\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\int_\Omega B\cdot\nabla\psi=0\text{ for every smooth scalar }\psi\text{ on }\overline\Omega\}.$$ This is the distributional divergence constraint together with weak zero normal flux; for smooth fields it is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $n\cdot B=0$. For every positive eigenvalue put $w_j=\operatorname{curl}u_j/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ and put $K_M=\{B\in M:\operatorname{curl}B=0\text{ distributionally}\}$. Then $$M=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j:\lambda_j>0\}}^{L^2}\mathbin{\oplus}K_M.$$ The declared first-order PEC modal energy class is $H\times M$, with weak modal equations $a_j'=v^2\sqrt{\lambda_j}b_j-\gamma a_j$, $b_j'=-\sqrt{\lambda_j}a_j$ for positive modes, $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$ for electric zero modes, and $(B,K_M)'=0$ for every kernel test. Define $D_M$ as the graph-norm completion of finite $w_j$ sums plus $K_M$, with norm squared $\|w\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}w\|_2^2$. The equivalent weak-in-time variational equations are $\langle E_t,\phi\rangle=v^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}\phi\rangle-\gamma\langle E,\phi\rangle$ for $\phi\in V$, and $\langle B_t,\psi\rangle=-\langle E,\operatorname{curl}\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in D_M$. They use the actual electric tangential-zero domain $V$ and magnetic normal-zero space $M$, with no claim of maximal-trace equality. For every initial pair in $H\times M$ there is a unique $C(\mathbb R;H\times M)$ solution of that declared realization, which also satisfies the displayed evolution equations distributionally in the interior. Finite electric and paired-magnetic modal sums, with the exact static magnetic kernel component retained, converge uniformly on compact time intervals in energy norm. No equality with every maximal rough tangential-trace realization is asserted.
(c) [Exact energy balance, decay and zero sectors] In both declared classes, for every $t_0<t_1$, $$\mathcal U(t_1)+\sigma\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\|E(t)\|_2^2\,dt=\mathcal U(t_0),\qquad \mathcal U'(t)=-\sigma\|E(t)\|_2^2\le0.$$ For positive smooth-cavity modes $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_ja_j=0$. If $\Delta_j=\gamma^2/4-v^2\lambda_j$ is positive, the two roots are $-\gamma/2\pm\sqrt{\Delta_j}$; if negative they are $-\gamma/2\pm i\sqrt{-\Delta_j}$; at zero include $(A+Bt)e^{-\gamma t/2}$. This finite scalar characteristic classification applies to every parameter $\lambda\ge0$ and uses no choice principle; its general zero-eigenvalue associated-wave solutions and the narrower first-order compatibility are stated separately in (d). The full Choice premise belongs to the smooth-cavity spectral realization, not to these finite root formulas. For $\sigma>0$ every positive mode decays, electric zero modes obey $a_j(t)=a_j(0)e^{-\gamma t}$, and magnetic kernel data stay constant. In the smooth class the solution therefore tends in energy norm as $t\to+\infty$ to $(0,P_{K_M}B(0))$. For $\sigma=0$ energy is constant, electric zero modes are static and the original lossless branch is recovered. The zero sectors are retained, not divided by their eigenvalues; no universal decay to zero in the presence of magnetic kernel data is claimed.
(d) [Associated second-order branch] Independently of first-order compatibility, the same spectral basis gives the damped associated electric wave for every $q_0\in V$, $q_1\in H$, with $q\in C(\mathbb R;V)$, $q'\in C(\mathbb R;H)$ and modal convergence uniformly on compact times. Its coefficients satisfy $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with arbitrary prescribed initial coefficients. At $\lambda_j=0$ they are $\alpha_j+\beta_j(1-e^{-\gamma t})/\gamma$ when $\gamma>0$, and $\alpha_j+t\beta_j$ when $\gamma=0$. Such arbitrary second-order data need not arise from the first-order Maxwell system: its zero modes additionally satisfy $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$. This broader wave is retained alongside the physical first-order branch. All square roots and real derivatives use [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the real-component exponential formula [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]].
(e) [Scope] The conductor occupies the declared cavity interior while its stationary walls obey the independent ideal PEC boundary model. No arbitrary loss tensor, memory law, changing interface, open-end, rough-wall or empirical conclusion is made. Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) suffices for the rectangular/Fourier branch; the smooth branch retains its actual full Choice premise. Weak energy balance is proved by modal limits and does not assert an unprovided nonlinear weak local Poynting theorem.

For (a), use the exact G2 product Fourier representation and parity constraints. Add the scalar term $-\gamma\widehat E$ to its finite real/imaginary matrix system. It is globally Lipschitz, so [[cor-globally-lipschitz-odes-have-global-solutions]] supplies a unique solution on all real time. Direct conjugate triple-product cancellation gives $(\varepsilon|\widehat E|^2+\mu^{-1}|\widehat B|^2)'=-2\sigma|\widehat E|^2$. Divergence constraints are preserved ($k\cdot\widehat E$ obeys $d'=-\gamma d$, $k\cdot\widehat B$ is constant), and damping preserves each original parity. Modal energy is nonincreasing forward and at most $e^{2\gamma T}$ times its initial value on $[-T,T]$, because its derivative is bounded below by $-2\gamma$ times itself; multiply by $e^{2\gamma t}$ and differentiate to prove that bound. Parseval therefore controls every omitted tail uniformly on compact times. Finite solutions converge in $C_tL^2$ and pass the linear distributional equations against compact-time smooth periodic tests by Cauchy-Schwarz, exactly as in G2. To identify the latter with $K_M$, take a compactly supported smooth vector test $\phi$. The actual smooth Dirichlet solver [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] with coefficient identity, zero trace and source $-\operatorname{div}\phi$ supplies $f\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)$ with $\Delta f=\operatorname{div}\phi$. The distributional compact-test pairing then gives $(B,w_j)=0$. Each paired modal system and every electric zero equation has unique global solutions; keep the given $K_M$ component exactly. The finite spectral tests are dense in $V$ with its G3 graph norm and in $D_M$ with its defined curl graph norm, so Cauchy-Schwarz passes the modal time-test equations to precisely the stated variational equations. Conversely testing those equations at $u_j$, $w_j$ and every $K_M$ vector gives the modal equations. The weak modal boundary realization therefore explicitly tests these spectral equations, so the scalar ODE uniqueness and complete decompositions give uniqueness in the stated class; merely satisfying interior equations without this boundary realization is not asserted sufficient. For strong first-order solutions with $E\in C^1_tH\cap C_tV$ and $B\in C^1_tL^2\cap C_tH(\operatorname{curl})$, the same collar pairing gives $a_j'=v^2(B,\operatorname{curl}u_j)-\gamma a_j$. Differentiating using $B'=-\operatorname{curl}E$ and the full-$X$ identity gives $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, with $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$ at zero eigenvalues.
For (c), sum the finite identities and integrate them on $[t_0,t_1]$. Uniform energy-norm convergence on that compact interval passes both energy and the continuous $\|E(t)\|_2^2$ integral to the limit, proving the exact balance. FTC then yields its derivative for every time. This argument proves rough finite-energy dissipation without using a smooth-only local balance; the smooth reading agrees with the restricted material-energy supplier. The characteristic roots follow by completing the square; their explicit real exponential or sine/cosine solutions are verified by the stated derivative suppliers. Repeated roots retain $te^{-\gamma t/2}$. after.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the constant isotropic material branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, $\sigma\ge0$, $J_{\rm ext}=0$ and initially zero volume charge. On the infinite straight rectangular guide $Q=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]], declare the finite-energy reflection class as follows. Extend in the two transverse variables to $T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R$, $T_{ab}^2=\mathbb R/(2a\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R/(2b\mathbb Z)$. The electric components have transverse parities even/odd, odd/even, odd/odd respectively; magnetic components have odd/even, even/odd, even/even respectively. (a) [Complete mixed transform] Let $\phi_{mn}(x_t)=(4ab)^{-1/2}e^{i\pi(mx_1/a+nx_2/b)}$, $(m,n)\in\mathbb Z^2$, be the orthonormal transverse characters. Write $\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)=\mathcal F_2F_{mn}(\xi)$ and $\beta=2\pi\xi$. The transform is a unitary representation of $L^2(T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R)$ by $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^2;L^2(\mathbb R))$, with inverse in $L^2$ from [[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]], and $$\|F\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=\tfrac14\sum_{m,n}\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)|^2\,d\xi$$ for these reflection fields. The parity and reality relations are retained, including $\widehat F_{-m,-n}(-\xi)=\overline{\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)}$. With $K=(\pi m/a,\pi n/b,2\pi\xi)$, the divergence constraints become $K\cdot\widehat E=K\cdot\widehat B=0$ for almost every $\xi$. (b) [Unique energy evolution] Adopt in that weak reflection class the constant-Ohmic first-order material evolution $E_t=v^2\operatorname{curl}B-\gamma E$, $B_t=-\operatorname{curl}E$, distributionally, consistent with the smooth [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] and [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]] branches. before.title: Spectral completeness of the declared PEC waveguide and cavity classes
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers. Let the PEC classes be those of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. Then:
(a) **Smooth cavity.** The curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace. For every chosen positive mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every displacement datum $q_0\in V$ and velocity datum $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$. Displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$, velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$, and finite modal sums converge in these respective norms uniformly on compact time intervals. The finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes remain $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The speed is a positive abstract parameter and has no physical dependency. The eigenfields are $C^\infty$ on the closure by [[lem-em-pec-cavity-eigenfield-boundary-regularity]], applied to the full-$X$ eigenvariational identity of the cavity supplier. The shifted scalar auxiliary boundary problems are solvable on the declared bounded smooth domain by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]]; the specific scalar Dirichlet resolvent and its smooth-zero-boundary test density used in G3 are supplied by its recorded local resolvent lemma.
(b) **Rectangular class.** For every rectangular box $Q=\prod_j(0,L_j)$ with $L_j>0$ and every pair of positive mathematical coefficients $\varepsilon,\mu>0$, the separable products described in the mode verification are dense in the reflection-parity energy class, and every initial datum of that class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy, with finite separated modes dense at every time. The rectangular statements are the recorded rectangular reflection-class completeness lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (the $G2$ branch); the individual TE/TM mode verification against the Maxwell equations and the PEC conditions is the recorded $G1$ physics branch, homed on the physical guide page and not consumed here as a mathematical premise. No completeness in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes is asserted.
before.strategy: The smooth-cavity spectral and finite-energy assertions are exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: its shifted coercive full-$X$ solution operator, divergence projection using the proved scalar Dirichlet resolvent and smooth-zero-boundary density, and compact self-adjoint spectral theorem give the complete $H^1$ graph-class eigenbasis, multiplicities, distributional equations and modal wave expansion with topology zero modes retained, for the explicitly quantified $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and arbitrary $V\times H$ data. The source distinguishes displacement $C(\mathbb R;V)$ from velocity $C(\mathbb R;H)$ with uniform convergence on compact time intervals; no unquantified physical speed is used. Each eigenfield satisfies its full-$X$ variational identity, so [[lem-em-pec-cavity-eigenfield-boundary-regularity]] gives the promised $C^\infty$ eigenfields on the closure, including $\lambda=0$. That supplier proves the coupled vector mixed boundary estimate and admissible tests in the chosen completion; the scalar [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] is used only for its actual scalar auxiliary boundary solvability and is not treated as a vector PEC regularity theorem. The quadratic graph forms and curl/div expressions use [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No classical smoothness of general finite-energy sums follows or is asserted. The rectangular assertions are unchanged [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (G2): reflection parities give the rectangular torus class; trigonometric product completeness and the finite-dimensional Fourier ODE conserve $\varepsilon|\hat E|^2+|\hat B|^2/\mu$, yielding the unique weak energy solution. The direct TE/TM verification G1 and uniform Ohmic-loss branch K10 remain physical branches on their own page, not mathematical premises here.
